routes.label: boc-3step-fc-ringclose-deprotect
routes.notes: 3-step route: FC acylation (2-engine support), ring-closing reductive amination (3-engine support), Boc deprotection (3-engine support). All leaves buyable. Bottleneck: cost score 0.73.

audit.reason: Claisen-type C-acylation of the cyclic ketone's alpha-CH2 with cyclopropanecarbonyl chloride (base/Mg enolate) gives the 2-acyl-1,3-diketone; carbons balance.

Knorr pyrazole condensation of a 2-acyl cycloalkanone with a monosubstituted hydrazine; ring gained is 5-membered and the regiochemistry (substituted N on the endocyclic ketone carbon) matches the classic 1-substituted tetrahydroindazole outcome.
Standard acidic Boc deprotection of the piperidine; Cdelta=-5 accounted for by loss of the Boc group.

audit.summary: All three steps are textbook transformations: C-acylation to a 1,3-diketone, Knorr-type pyrazole annulation with an N-aminopiperidine hydrazine, and Boc removal. Carbon counts and ring changes are fully consistent, and the pyrazole regiochemistry matches the known behavior of 2-acylcycloalkanones with monosubstituted hydrazines.

routes.label: n-alkylation-3bromopiperidine-hydrazine-3step
routes.notes: 3-bromopiperidine variant of N-alkylation route. Lower feasibility than mesylate variant. ChemBART support for N-alkylation.

routes.notes: N-alkylation with piperidin-3-ol (USPTO:6389, rank 1 template). Higher greenness (0.8487) than mesylate variant. Lower feasibility than Boc ring-closure.
